text:
tara: FYI pushed a perf/oom rabbit hole from last night's canary into staging. p99 latency up ~6% on longctx workloads, plus a couple transient OOMs. attaching quick flame and alloc log.
max: can you paste the profile? is this after the kernel-chooser change that prefers flashattn for short kvs?
tara: yeah that change landed yesterday. profiling gist: `alloc_trace.txt` show a lot more small allocs and free churn around attention + ffn boundaries. also noticed KV cache evictions spiking right before OOMs.
jorge: hmm sounds like fragmentation. did kernel chooser change allocate different workspace sizes? flashattn v1.3 uses separate temp buffers vs v1.2 which reused ffn scratch, afaik.
lin: i pulled the staging trace: flashattn path requests ~1.12x workspace for our typical L=2048 windows (because of padding align to 128). cuBLASLt path used more fused workspace but with fewer small allocs.
max: that would explain p99; more churn -> allocator pressure -> slower kernels due to stalls. what's allocator config on dedicated nodes? slab size?
tara: currently slab=32MB per device, grow-on-demand, top-level mmap for huge arenas. headroom multiplier was historically 1.1 for safety. after the kernel-chooser change we didn't bump headroom.
jorge: proposal: introduce a narrow playbook for headroom + fallback thresholds: 1) leader-only pre-reserve slab bump to 64MB for attention heavy batches, 2) headroom multiplier from 1.1->1.18 for attention/ffn combined path, 3) kernel fallback: if flash workspace > 0.95*available_slab then force cuBLASLt fallback.
lin: +1 but also consider opportunistic buffer reuse at runtime: reuse ffn scratch for flash temp if same lifetime. cheap heuristic: if last_free_chunk_size >= needed && last_alloc_ts - now < 50ms reuse instead of fresh alloc.
max: can we do that without touching allocator internals? maybe add a tiny pooling layer inside runtime that tracks last scratch ptr per-stream and tries reuse. cheaper and lower-risk than allocator patches.
tara: i prototyped a small pool. results: p99 down ~3% in local microbench but not yet under KV-heavy mixes. KV evict pattern seems to be the trigger: when cache slices evict, free bursts clobber pool and we end up back to fragmented allocations.
jorge: then we need soft-reserve for KV cache: keep a tiny reserve slab (per-GPU) that KV can't touch unless under pressure. e.g. mark 8MB reserved for runtime temporary allocations. If KV eviction is needed, prefer LRU within KV before touching reserved.
lin: config snippet suggestion: `
rt.runtime: 
  headroom_multiplier: 1.18
  per_gpu_reserved_temp: 8MB
  slab_size_hint: 64MB
  kernel_fallback_threshold: 0.95
`
max: sounds reasonable. one more: telemetry. add counters for: workspace_alloc_calls, alloc_fail_retros, kernel_fallbacks_triggered, kv_eviction_count_per_request. we need to correlate OOM with kv eviction spikes.
ci-bot: deploy started: runtime/chooser-playbook/HEAD -> staging (sha: b7f3c). smoke tests running.
sre-bot: alert suppressed: p99 increased on staging; investigating correlated alloc spikes.
tara: next steps: 1) roll the small pooling change + headroom bump to staging behind feature flag, 2) add telemetry counters, 3) run longctx soak with mixed KV pressure load for 6 hours, 4) if stable, flip kernel fallback threshold to 0.9 and re-run to measure cost/perf tradeoff.
jorge: also add a microprof that records per-request peak_alloc and sequence of kernel choices, then postprocess to find patterns like "flash chosen + kv-evict -> OOM". that will let us autotune fallback threshold per-model.
lin: note: lowering fallback threshold will push more requests to cuBLASLt which increases token cost ~2-4% on some shapes. we should gate by cost-slo tag.
max: i can instrument the cost-slo tag and add an automated A/B: fallback 0.95 vs 0.9 on canary fleet. measure p99 and token cost delta.
tara: thanks. i'll open a tiny RFC with playbook + rollout plan and link benchmark artifacts. ci-bot: please post run ids once staging soak completes. :+1:
max: ping me when RFC is up, i'll hook up the telemetry dashboards.
jorge: also let's add an evict-rollback safety: if a request triggers eviction and then allocation fails, roll back eviction decisions (re-commit KV slices) and force a graceful fallback to smaller batch or deny with clear error so callers can retry. reduces hard OOM fallout.
tara: good call. that rollback is low-risk and helps customer UX. OK i'm going to land the flag and start the soak. will update thread with staging run ids.
ci-bot: staging-run: r-2026-03-18-007 started (soak target 6h).
sre-bot: monitoring rule created: alloc_spike_warning -> paging to #eng-runtime if sustained for 5m.
max: nice. if we see stable numbers after soak, we can bake defaults for Dedicated in next release.
tara: thanks all — appreciate the quick triage.
